f: Uzbek plov (palov, plov): yellow rice pilaf with carrots and meat pieces on top, sometimes chickpeas, raisins, garlic
baked samsa (samsa): triangular or square golden tandoor pastry with meat and onion, crisp flaky top, sometimes sesame
manti: LARGE steamed dumplings (5–8 cm, about 55 g each), thin translucent dough gathered on top, usually 4–6 on a plate, often with sour cream
chuchvara: SMALL boiled dumplings like pelmeni (pelmen), 2–3 cm, many (15–30) in a bowl or plate, without broth
fried laghman / Uyghur laghman: thick hand-pulled noodles on a plate topped with stir-fried meat, peppers, celery and sauce, no broth
naryn: very thin finely cut cold noodles mixed with finely sliced boiled horse meat or beef, served as a heap
dimlama: stew of large chunks of meat, potatoes, cabbage, carrots, peppers and tomatoes
kazan kebab: fried meat pieces with golden fried potato wedges, often with onion rings
grilled beef or lamb chunks on a skewer (shashlik), usually with raw onion
lula kebab: long minced-meat sausage-shaped kebab on a skewer
khanum: steamed dough roll with meat, potato or pumpkin filling, cut into wide spiral slices
dolma: stuffed bell pepper, cabbage roll or grape-leaf roll filled with rice and minced meat
tandoor baked lamb or beef pieces
qovurma: fried meat chunks with onion
moshkichiri: thick mung bean and rice porridge with meat
kutab: thin flat half-moon flatbread folded over a filling, pan-fried
gumma / pirozhki: oval DEEP-FRIED dough pastries, smooth brown surface, meat or potato inside
tukhum barak: boiled dumplings filled with egg
shurpa (shurva, shorva): clear meat soup with large pieces of potato, carrot and meat
mastava: rice soup with meat and vegetables, rice visible in broth, often with sour cream
laghman (lagman) soup: thick hand-pulled noodles in a bowl with broth and meat-vegetable sauce
mung bean and rice soup, thick, with small green mung beans visible
chuchvara soup: many small dumplings floating in broth in a kosa bowl
ugra: homemade noodle soup with meat
roasted, grilled or boiled chicken pieces with skin
skinless chicken breast, boiled or grilled
meat cutlet / meatball (kotlet, tefteli), fried or stewed; may have a quail egg inside (part of the cutlet)
kazy: horse meat sausage, round dark slices with a white fat ring, often on top of plov
shivit oshi: bright green dill noodles topped with meat and vegetable stew (Khorezm)
pasta or macaroni mixed with fried minced meat
fried eggs or scrambled eggs cooked with tomatoes in a pan
slice of bread with butter, cheese or sausage on top
Samarkand non: thick heavy glossy round flatbread, about 500 g whole
shirchoy: tea with milk, butter and salt in a bowl
small quail egg, about 3 cm, about 10 g, often placed on top of plov
sweet rice porridge cooked in milk
boiled mung beans, beans or chickpeas
Uzbek round flatbread non (lepyoshka); one quarter piece
patir: rich layered flatbread with fat
baursak: small puffy deep fried dough squares or balls
achichuk: thin sliced tomato and onion salad served with plov
Tashkent salad: radish, beef, egg, mayonnaise
fresh cucumber, tomato, greens salad with oil
ayran: salted yogurt drink with water
chak-chak: small fried dough pieces stuck together with honey in a mound
cup of green or black tea without sugar
sweet tea with two teaspoons of sugar
shawarma wrap (called lavash in Uzbekistan) with meat, fries and sauce
deep fried chicken wings, strips or nuggets

ai.rules:
Rules:
- A cooked dish counts as ONE item. Never list its visible ingredients separately: the meat, vegetables, herbs and sauce on laghman are part of the laghman; meat pieces on top of plov are part of the plov (id "osh"); an egg inside a meatball or cabbage roll is part of it.
- Separate garnishes placed on top of a plate ARE listed separately: plov is often garnished with whole quail eggs and slices of kazy, so look carefully at the top and edges of a plov plate.
- Small whole white or speckled eggs about 3 cm long are quail eggs (id "bedana_tuxum", about 10 g each). Count them: g = count x 10.
- Round slices of sausage with a white fat ring are kazy (id "qazi", about 30 g per slice). They are not butter.
- For countable foods (eggs, somsa, manti, skewers, dolma, meatballs, pieces of bread) estimate g as count x typical weight.
- If several people eat from one big shared dish (a lagan) or from a shared table (dasturxon), give the TOTAL weight of each dish as it is in the photo and set shared: true. The app then asks how many people ate and divides.
- Include side salads, bread and drinks if they are visible.
- Do not list oil, butter or sauces that are mixed into a dish and cannot be seen separately.
